title: Find the ~12 MB/s ceiling between Cloudflare and the server
description: 2026-10-26, owner's Mac on (likely) Wi-Fi: back-to-back, Mac -> Cloudflare (speed.cloudflare.com, HTTP/1.1) 30-35 MB/s vs Mac -> cellcounts /healthz (HTTP/3, full body through tunnel, nginx request_time matches browser time) 11-14 MB/s. Ruled out: cloudflared CPU (30-38% of its 1-CPU cap, never throttled), nginx/web CPU, NAS (103 MB/s), server download from Cloudflare (44 MB/s), UDP receive-buffer drops (RcvbufErrors 0 over 2.4M datagrams, though rmem_max is the 208 KiB default and quic-go wanted 7 MiB). Browser and tunnel both use DFW. Next, on a wired gigabit connection: A/B cloudflared --protocol quic vs http2; HTTP/3 on/off for the zone; 1 vs 3 vs 6 parallel; watch LaneTuner's choice during a real upload.
notes: Found 2026-10-26 (owner's Mac wired, same LAN as the server, so tests hairpin through the home uplink; home upload measured 66-86 MB/s with 3 streams): cloudflared over QUIC capped uploads at ~13-25 MB/s regardless of parallelism; --protocol http2 gave 23-30 MB/s (1 at a time), 38-55 (3), 42-64 (6), A-B-A-B. Chrome (HTTP/3 to the edge) through the http2 tunnel: 27-29 (1), 33-35 (3/6); curl over ONE shared HTTP/2 connection: 38 (1), 60 (3) -> turning HTTP/3 off for the zone would likely help browsers further (owner's dashboard call; zone-wide). Live app upload of 2.0 GB: ~29 MB/s average; exposed a LaneTuner bug (never left 2 lanes), fixed.
close_reason: Found: cloudflared over QUIC capped uploads at ~13-25 MB/s; HTTP/2 tunnel (e1d4d04) gives 23-30 (1 stream) to 55-64 MB/s (6). Also fixed nginx pinning the web container's old address after a deploy (26babdc). Browser-side HTTP/3 remains a cap (~30-35 MB/s in Chrome) - see follow-up.

title: Parallel chunk uploads, adapted to the connection
description: Measured 2026-10-26: one upload stream from the owner's Mac reaches ~13 MB/s to Cloudflare, three streams ~23 MB/s; the server side takes ~44 MB/s from Cloudflare and the NAS writes ~103 MB/s. The uploader sends one 32 MB chunk at a time, so it leaves ~40% of the uplink unused. Send several chunks at once, with the count adjusted to the connection (grow while throughput improves, shrink when it doesn't or chunks get slow), keeping per-chunk time far from Cloudflare's ~100 s limit. Server must accept concurrent, out-of-order chunks safely. Also explain the 400 on a chunk PUT seen at 03:26 UTC.
notes: Built: LaneTuner (frontend/src/workspace/uploads/laneTuner.ts) + parallel lanes in uploader.ts; 33 frontend tests; local run of 3 x 277 MB: 2 chunks in flight, all images passed the server hash check. Not yet deployed. The 400 at 03:26 UTC was the page being left mid-chunk (status polling stopped at the same second; leave-page warning already exists).
close_reason: Live on production. After the sampling fix (21d0d1c) the tuner tried 3 lanes at ~9 s, saw no gain over 2 in Chrome (HTTP/3 to the edge caps ~30-35 MB/s), went back to 2 at ~20 s; 2.0 GB uploaded at ~30 MB/s.

title: Consider turning off HTTP/3 for the zone (browser upload ceiling)
description: With the tunnel on HTTP/2, Chrome uploads top out ~30-35 MB/s over its single HTTP/3 connection to Cloudflare; curl over one shared HTTP/2 connection reached 38 MB/s (1 at a time) and ~60 MB/s (3 at a time) on the same path (2026-10-26, owner's LAN). Turning off 'HTTP/3 (with QUIC)' in the Cloudflare dashboard (Speed/Network) would likely let browsers use HTTP/2 and let LaneTuner find gains from more lanes. The setting is zone-wide (all of matthewbolding.com), so it's the owner's call; re-measure in Chrome after (alt-svc caching may need a browser restart).
